title: 2001 AMC 8 Problem 23
statement: Points \(R,\) \(S\) and \(T\) are vertices of an equilateral triangle, and points \(X,\) \(Y\) and \(Z\) are midpoints of its sides. How many noncongruent triangles can be drawn using any three of these six points as vertices?

solutions.text:
Using the side length of the small equilateral triangles as one unit, the possible triangle side-length patterns are:

equilateral with sides \(2,2,2\); equilateral with sides \(1,1,1\); small isosceles with sides \(1,1,\sqrt3\); and larger isosceles with sides \(1,\sqrt3,2\).

These four patterns all occur in the figure, and symmetry shows every triangle formed by three of the six points matches one of them.

Thus there are \(4\) noncongruent triangles.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Use symmetry to avoid recounting congruent cases
